name: Cough with a cold
transcript:
Thanks — you said you are coughing.
To continue the screening, what is your age in years?

You said you are coughing. Is the person conscious, breathing normally, and able to respond to call?
OPTIONS: Yes - conscious, breathing normally and responding | Cardiac arrest | Not breathing | Unresponsive | Not responding to call | Confused, agitated or disoriented | Altered mental state or not fully conscious | Obvious neurological deficits | None of these | Not sure
Yes - conscious, breathing normally and responding

You said you are coughing, 30 years old, and are awake and breathing normally. Is there any bleeding or injury? (Includes vomiting or coughing up blood, heavy periods, nosebleeds or a known bleeding disorder.)
OPTIONS: No bleeding or injury | Yes | Not sure

You said you are coughing and are breathing normally. Is there any trouble breathing right now, such as breathlessness, wheezing or noisy breathing? (A cough or blocked nose alone does not count.)
OPTIONS: No - breathing comfortably | Yes - some trouble breathing | Not sure

Thanks — one quick check: Is the skin pale or bluish, with cold hands and feet?
OPTIONS: Yes | No | Not sure

Thanks — you said you're coughing and breathing comfortably. Is there chest pain or other pain? How severe is it on a scale of 0 to 10?
OPTIONS: Severe chest pain | Severe pain (8-10) | Moderate pain (4-7) | Mild pain (1-3) | No pain (0) | None of these | Not sure

You said you're coughing and breathing comfortably. Which of these describe the breathing problem?
OPTIONS: Stridor - harsh, high-pitched noise when breathing in | Increased work of breathing and feeling tired | Agitation or anxiety with breathing difficulty | Slow breaths or poor respiratory effort | Breathless with change of voice | Rapid breaths | Wheezing, but able to talk in sentences | Wheezing in a known asthmatic | Hyperventilation | Mild or minimal breathlessness | Comfortable, no other symptoms | None of these | Not sure

You said you're coughing, 30 years old and breathing comfortably. Do any of these apply?
OPTIONS: Non-stop coughing fits, unable to catch breath between them | Blue lips or skin (cyanotic spells) | Unable to swallow | Has to sit leaning forward on the hands to breathe (tripod position) | Something stuck in the airway | Has needed a breathing tube or ICU care for breathing before | None of these | Not sure

You said you are coughing and breathing comfortably. Is the person having a seizure, or unable to sit, stand, walk or communicate?
OPTIONS: Ongoing seizures | Cannot sit or stand unsupported | Cannot stand or walk unsupported | Cannot communicate | Alert, walking and talking normally | None of these | Not sure

You said you're coughing, 30 years old, and breathing comfortably. Is the person in respiratory distress (struggling to breathe)?
OPTIONS: Yes | No | Not sure

Thanks — quick follow-up: Is there an abnormal noise with every breath, such as a harsh high-pitched sound, gurgling or snoring? (A cough, phlegm you can cough up, or a blocked nose does not count.)
OPTIONS: Yes | No | Not sure

You said you're coughing, 30 years old, breathing comfortably and alert. Are the symptoms only mild upper respiratory (cold-like) symptoms while tolerating oral intake?
OPTIONS: Yes | No | Not sure

You said you have a mild cough, are breathing comfortably and alert. Is the person less alert than normal?
OPTIONS: Yes | No | Not sure

You said you're coughing, breathing comfortably and alert. Is there an abnormal noise with every breath, such as a harsh high-pitched sound, gurgling or snoring? (A cough, phlegm you can cough up, or a blocked nose does not count.)
OPTIONS: Yes | No | Not sure

You said you have a mild cough and are breathing comfortably. Is the person in respiratory distress (struggling to breathe)?
OPTIONS: Yes | No | Not sure

Level 4 - Early Care
Level 4 - Early Care (target: under 60 minutes). Needs medical care soon: go to an Emergency Department or a walk-in / urgent-care clinic.
Key findings: Mild upper respiratory (cold-like) symptoms; tolerating oral intake.
What to do now: Seek assessment at an ED or urgent-care clinic within 60 minutes.
If symptoms worsen (new or increasing breathlessness, noisy breathing, blue lips/skin, fainting, severe chest pain, or becoming very drowsy/unresponsive), call 999 immediately.
This is a preliminary screening, not a medical diagnosis. It does not replace assessment by a healthcare professional. If symptoms worsen, call 999.
